segments.text:
I.
WHEN firſt thy gracious Eye's ſurvey,
Ev'n in the midſt of Youth and Night,
Mark'd me, where ſunk in Sin I lay;
I felt a ſtrange unknown Delight.

II.
My Soul in all its Pow'rs renew'd
Own'd the Divine Phyſician's Art,
So ſwift the Healing Look bedew'd,
Embalm'd, o'er-ran and fill'd my Heart.

III.
Since then I many a bitter Storm
Have felt, and feeling ſure had dy'd,
Had the malicious Fatal Harm
Roll'd on its unmoleſted Tide:

IV.
But working ſtill, within my Soul,
Thy ſweet Original Joy remain'd;
Thy Love did all my Griefs controul,
Thy Love the Victory more than gain'd.

V.
If the firſt Glance, but open'd now
And now ſeal'd up, ſo pow'rful prove,
What wondrous Tranſports ſhall we know
When glorying in thy full-ey'd Love!

VI.
When Thou ſhalt look us out of Pain,
And raiſe us to thy Bliſsful Sight,
With open Face ſtrong to ſuſtain
The Blaze of thy unclouded Light!
